title: Batch assignment
$comment: What the runtime cut from the approved inventory and handed to one generator call. Written by the runtime rather than by a model, so the assignment is auditable independently of the answer it produced.

resolverOwnedPaths.$comment: Approved paths deliberately withheld from every batch because a resolver produces them. Named so the omission reads as a decision rather than as a gap the generator should fill.

allApprovedPaths.$comment: Every approved path, not only this batch's. A batch that may import a helper another batch is writing needs to know the helper exists, or it invents a second copy.

layer.$comment: How deep this batch sits in the dependency graph of the approved inventory. Layer zero depends on nothing the run writes; every layer above it is asked only once the layers below have answered.

dependsOnBatchIds.$comment: The batches that wrote the files this one builds on. Their answers are supplied with this assignment, so an import here is checked against text rather than against intent.

repairInstructions.$comment: Present only when a review asked for a targeted repair. What each reviewer wants changed in the files this batch owns, in the reviewer's own words.

carriedDependencies.$comment: Paths of files this batch has to keep agreeing with that are not being regenerated: its dependencies and the callers a targeted repair left alone. The bodies are supplied as a separate artifact named by carriedDependencyArtifact, so this assignment stays small enough to be read inline.

carriedDependencyArtifact.$comment: The name of the artifact holding the final text of every path in carriedDependencies. Empty when nothing is carried forward.
